encounters.cc: Persistent fatigue, generalized weakness, erectile difficulty, and morning knee discomfort

lines: Persistent fatigue, generalized weakness, erectile difficulty, and morning knee discomfort
That has slowly worsened over the past year.
He reports new-onset erectile difficulty and mild discomfort in his knees, especially in the mornings.
He also notes having an unusually dry mouth that occasionally interferes with eating.
On further questioning, he states that he has not been active and spends most of his time indoors, yet he has developed what he calls a "strange tan" that others have commented on.
He denies any use of tanning products, new medications, or recent sun exposure.
Family history is notable for a brother who developed cirrhosis at a relatively young age.
He has no history of travel, alcohol use, or illicit drugs.
Physical examination reveals mild hepatomegaly and bronzed pigmentation over the face, arms, and upper torso.
Joint examination is significant for limited range of motion at the second and third MCP joints with tenderness.
Laboratory evaluation shows mildly elevated liver enzymes and elevated fasting blood glucose.

encounters.cc: Progressive swelling in lower legs and increasing fatigue with foamy, dark urine

lines: Progressive swelling in lower legs and increasing fatigue with foamy, dark urine

This 45-year-old male with hereditary hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, and chronic kidney disease stage 3, previously evaluated in January for fatigue and joint discomfort, returns to clinic with his wife reporting progressive swelling in his lower legs and increasing fatigue over the past month.
He also reports that his urine has been "foamy" and occasionally darker than usual.
The patient was diagnosed with Wilson disease 6 years ago after presenting with abnormal liver function tests and neurologic symptoms, including mild dysarthria and tremor.
Since diagnosis, he has been managed with dietary copper restriction and a chelating agent.
His dose of the chelating agent was increased 5 months ago due to rising urinary copper levels on follow-up testing.
He has been adherent to all medications and has not recently started any new drugs.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 8 years ago.
Alcohol: History of chronic alcohol use disorder, currently abstinent for 3 years.
On examination, temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure is 130/78 mm Hg, pulse is 78/min, and respiratory rate is 16/min.
Physical exam reveals periorbital puffiness and 2+ bilateral pitting edema to the mid-shins.
Cardiopulmonary examination is normal, and there are no rashes or joint swelling.
Abdominal exam shows mild hepatomegaly without tenderness or ascites.
No pulmonary crackles are heard, and there is no jugular venous distension.
Laboratory studies show a serum creatinine of 0.9 mg/dL and serum albumin of 2.2 g/dL Urinalysis shows 4+ protein, no red blood cells, no white blood cells and no casts.
Immunofluorescence demonstrates fine granular deposits of IgG and C3 along the glomerular capillary wall.

encounters.cc: One-week history of burning sensation in mouth and difficulty tasting food

lines: One-week history of burning sensation in mouth and difficulty tasting food
He returns for follow-up of hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, and membranous nephropathy.
He recently completed a 10-day oral antibiotic course for community-acquired pneumonia.
His medical history is notable for well-controlled type 2 diabetes.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 8 years ago.
Alcohol: History of chronic alcohol use disorder, currently abstinent for 3 years.
Physical examination reveals multiple creamy white plaques on the buccal mucosa and tongue that can be scraped off, leaving an erythematous base.
A potassium hydroxide preparation of a scraping reveals budding yeast with pseudohyphae.
The patient is prescribed a topical antifungal that is administered as an oral suspension, which he is instructed to swish in the mouth and swallow several times daily for 1–2 weeks.

encounters.cc: Two-day history of pain, redness, fever, and chills in left arm following hand laceration at work

lines: Two-day history of pain, redness, fever, and chills in left arm following hand laceration at work
This 47-year-old male with hereditary hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, type 2 diabetes, and cirrhosis, previously evaluated for oral candidiasis, presents with fever and chills.
He reports a minor laceration on his left hand that occurred 3 days ago while working.
He initially cleaned the wound with water but did not seek further medical attention.
His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, well-controlled on metformin.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 8 years ago.
Alcohol: History of chronic alcohol use disorder, currently abstinent for 3 years.
His temperature is 38.5°C (101.3°F), heart rate is 100 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg.
On physical examination, there is a 5 cm erythematous, tender streak extending proximally from the wound on his left hand.
There is also palpable tenderness in the left axillary region.

encounters.cc: Severe sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and muffled voice for 24 hours

lines: Severe sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and muffled voice for 24 hours

This 47-year-old male with hereditary hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, cirrhosis, CKD stage 3, and type 2 diabetes, evaluated in April 2022 for drug-induced hemolytic anemia post-lymphangitis, returns to the emergency department with a 24-hour history of severe sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and a muffled voice.
He mentions a recent bout of the common cold, which he thought had resolved.
He has not been able to swallow his saliva and has not taken his diabetes medications since yesterday.
- Acute lymphangitis of left upper limb (diagnosed 2022-03-15)
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 8 years ago.
Alcohol: History of chronic alcohol use disorder, currently abstinent for 3 years.
He is febrile with a temperature of 38.9°C (102°F), heart rate of 110 bpm, and respiratory rate of 22 breaths/min
On examination, he appears anxious, is sitting upright, and is leaning forward.
He has significant tenderness on palpation of the anterior neck, and you note the presence of stridor and drooling.
His blood glucose level is 250 mg/dL
A lateral neck radiograph is obtained and shows a swollen epiglottis with the characteristic "thumbprint" sign.

encounters.cc: Increasing pain and swelling in neck with difficulty swallowing and speaking

lines: Increasing pain and swelling in neck with difficulty swallowing and speaking

The patient is a 47-year-old male with hereditary hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, cirrhosis, and recent history of lymphangitis and upper airway infection, who presents to the emergency department with a 2-day history of increasing pain and swelling in his neck.
He reports that the pain began in a tooth and has since spread.
He has difficulty swallowing and speaking.
- Acute lymphangitis of left upper limb (diagnosed 2022-03-15)
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 8 years ago.
Alcohol: History of chronic alcohol use disorder, currently abstinent for 3 years.
On examination, the patient is febrile with a temperature of 38.9°C (102°F), heart rate of 110 bpm, and respiratory rate of 22 breaths per minute.
Oxygen saturation on room air is 94%.
There is marked brawny edema of the upper neck and submandibular area, with tenderness to palpation.
The patient is drooling and has difficulty protruding his tongue, which appears to be displaced posteriorly.
White blood cell count: 18,000 /µL, Neutrophils: 80%, Blood glucose: 250 mg/dL

encounters.cc: Two-day history of hematemesis and melena

lines: Two-day history of hematemesis and melena
The patient is a 48-year-old male with hereditary hemochromatosis, Wilson disease, and cirrhosis who presents with a two-day history of hematemesis and melena.
He has a history of membranous nephropathy and prior severe infections including Ludwig angina.
He reports no recent trauma or use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.
- Acute lymphangitis of left upper limb (diagnosed 2022-03-15)
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 8 years ago.
Alcohol: History of chronic alcohol use disorder, currently abstinent for 3 years.
On examination, he is jaundiced with multiple spider angiomas on his chest and an enlarged, tender liver edge palpable below the right costal margin.
His abdomen is distended with a fluid wave consistent with ascites.
